notes.meaning: Snow during hot summer weather is out of place, and rain during harvest ruins the grain. In the same way, giving high honor or public praise to a fool does not fit and only leads to trouble. It confirms the fool in his bad habits and gives him power to do harm.

A small bird flutters around and flies past without landing, and a swallow keeps moving in the air. In the same way, a curse spoken against an innocent person has no power to harm him. God governs what happens, so unfair and spiteful words will not take effect.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The traditional Catholic Douay-Rheims translation reads this verse as saying that an undeserved curse will indeed come upon a person, which older commentators understood as rebounding upon the one who spoke it.

notes.meaning: Horses and donkeys require whips and bridles to make them move in the right direction. A foolish person acts like a stubborn animal because he refuses to listen to reason. He will only learn when painful consequences force him to stop his harmful behavior.

Do not sink to a foolish person's level by copying his silly arguments, bad temper, or ugly insults. Joining in his foolish speech only makes you look just as foolish as he is. Wise people keep their self-control when confronted by unreasonable talk.

There are moments when a fool needs to be answered directly so his errors can be exposed. Giving a sharp, wise correction keeps him from boasting and thinking he is clever. Wise answers can protect others from being misled by his nonsense.

Sending an important message through a foolish person is as damaging as cutting off your own feet. The sender expects the work to be done, but the fool fails to carry it out properly. The person who trusted him ends up suffering deep loss and embarrassment.

A wise saying in the mouth of a fool is as useless and awkward as limp legs hanging from a man who cannot walk. The fool may repeat clever words, but he does not understand them or live by them. Speaking wisdom he does not practice only makes him look ridiculous.

Tying a rock tightly into a sling defeats the whole purpose of the weapon because the stone cannot be launched properly. Giving public respect or authority to a fool is just as useless and unfitting. The honor is completely wasted on someone who cannot use it well.

A proverb handled by a fool is like a sharp thorn branch waved around by a drunk person. Because he lacks good sense, he cannot control the wise saying properly and ends up hurting both himself and those around him. Good advice is dangerous when handled without understanding.

Hiring a fool or an untrained stranger to do an important task is like an archer shooting arrows wildly into a crowd. Random harm is sure to follow when careless people are put into positions of responsibility. Leaders must take great care in whom they choose to employ.

A dog returns to the very vomit that made it sick in the first place. In the same disgusting way, a foolish person repeats his wicked choices even after feeling their painful and shameful results. Sinners who refuse to change their hearts keep slipping back into their old habits.

A proud person who is convinced of his own wisdom is in worse danger than an ordinary fool. A simple fool might eventually recognize his ignorance and accept help, but a proud person refuses all teaching. Pride completely closes the mind against learning from God or others.

A lazy person makes up wild excuses to avoid going outside to do honest work, claiming a fierce lion is roaming the city streets. He imagines extreme and unlikely dangers so he can justify staying indoors. Sloth makes people creative only when inventing reasons not to do their duty.

A door swings back and forth on its hinges without ever traveling anywhere. A lazy man does the same thing as he rolls from one side to the other in bed, completely tied to his place of rest. He uses plenty of motion, but he never actually makes any progress in life.

The lazy man dips his hand into the food bowl but finds it too exhausting to lift it back to his mouth. This extreme and humorous picture shows how laziness can rob a person of even the desire to care for his own needs. Neglect eventually ruins the person who refuses to make an effort.

The lazy person arrogantly believes he is smarter than seven sensible people who can explain their sound judgments. Because he avoids the hard work of learning, he mistakes his stubborn opinions for genuine wisdom. Laziness often produces an unteachable sense of self-importance.

Stepping in to meddle with a fight that does not concern you is as dangerous as grabbing a stray dog by the ears. It is hard to keep holding on, and letting go invites a painful bite. Wise people avoid inserting themselves into other people's private arguments.

A person who deceives his neighbor and then tries to laugh it off by saying he was only joking is like a madman shooting flaming arrows and deadly weapons. Reckless lies cause deep damage, regardless of how lightly the liar treats them. Claiming a trick was just a prank does not erase the pain and ruin it brings.

A fire quickly dies out when it runs completely out of wood to burn. In the very same way, bitter arguments settle down and vanish when gossips stop spreading rumors. Refusing to repeat tales brings peace to homes and communities.

Charcoal feeds glowing embers and wood keeps a fire blazing hot. A quarrelsome person acts just like that fuel, constantly stoking arguments and keeping angry feelings alive. Such people love conflict and make every small disagreement worse.

Gossip seems like delicious, sweet food that people eagerly take in and enjoy. Yet once those whispered words are swallowed, they sink deep inside the heart and leave lasting wounds that are hard to heal. Slander leaves a mark long after the conversation is over.

Warm, affectionate words spoken from an evil heart are like a shiny layer of silver glaze painted over cheap clay pottery. The outside looks bright and valuable, but the inside remains base and worthless. Smooth speech often hides selfish and hateful motives.

A person who harbors hatred often covers it up by using polite and friendly words. While his speech sounds pleasant, he is quietly storing up deceit inside his heart. He waits for the right moment to strike against the person he secretly despises.

Do not believe a malicious man when he speaks with a gentle and persuasive voice. His heart is overflowing with all kinds of wickedness, represented by the number seven, which means complete fullness. People should stay on guard against dishonest flattery.

Even though a person conceals his malice beneath clever pretenses, his evil character will eventually be shown out in the open. A time of public reckoning will uncover his real intentions before the community. Deceit can only hide wicked plans for a little while.

Anyone who digs a hidden pit to trap another person will end up falling into it himself. Rolling a heavy boulder up a hill to crush someone else will result in the stone rolling back down to crush the one who pushed it. God ensures that traps set for others often catch the people who made them.

A liar naturally detests the very people he has damaged with his slander. Meanwhile, smooth flattery works secretly to build up pride and bring about someone's downfall. Both slander and fake compliments are dangerous tools that lead to ruin.
